acceptance: Payroll obligations wake only when employees > 0: with the employees fact set to 1 and a first-hire date saved, sync creates filings for Form 941, Form 940, W-2s, Colorado withholding, Colorado UI, FAMLI and the new Colorado new-hire report; at employees 0 none of them apply or create filings.

Colorado new-hire report (co.payroll.new_hire): due the first employee's start date plus 20 calendar days, GUIDED_WEB with the federal state-directory link; with employees > 0 but no start date recorded it stays unscheduled with the reason printed, never an invented date.

Hiring checklist on the Compliance screen (employees > 0 only): EIN, W-4, I-9, new hire report, Colorado withholding account, UI account, FAMLI registration, workers' comp policy, workplace posters, paid sick leave — each with plain words, the official link, and dates where a date exists; state derives from the business facts and filings (EIN recorded, new-hire filing state), never honor-system ticks.

Decisions question DQ-CMP-PAYROLL-HOW filed (starting value: payroll service — the careful choice, tax tables change often and payroll errors carry penalties); the in-app payroll engine is designed only if Chris chooses it.

Payroll provider CSV import: a summary file (pay_date, gross_wages, employer_taxes, amount_withdrawn, optional employee_taxes and provider) posts one balanced books journal per pay run through writeJournal as source type PAYROLL — Dr wages, Dr employer payroll taxes, Cr bank — against new system accounts WAGES (Schedule C line 26) and EMPLOYER_PAYROLL_TAXES (line 23); unbalanced rows refuse the file with plain words and post nothing; re-importing the same file is stopped by the (fileHash, rowIndex) uniqueness and posts nothing twice; importing before the books start date refuses with a plain message; a PayrollImport record keeps each row's totals with no employee-level personal data anywhere.
ci green at the exact head; every review comment read and answered.
invariants: Payroll obligations apply only when the employees fact is > 0; at 0 they stay dormant with the CMP-1 'wakes up when you hire' wording and create no filings.

The new-hire report deadline is the first employee's start date plus 20 calendar days (the verified Colorado rule); no date is ever invented — employees > 0 without a start date leaves the obligation unscheduled with the reason printed.
The hiring checklist stores no checkbox state; every status shown derives from facts or filings.

The payroll CSV import posts only balanced journals through the books engine (writeJournal) as source type PAYROLL: Dr wages (gross), Dr employer payroll taxes, Cr bank (amount withdrawn). A row that cannot balance — the provider's one withdrawal must equal gross + employer taxes, the employee share riding inside the gross — posts nothing and names the line.
Re-importing the same file never double-posts: (fileHash, rowIndex) is unique and writeJournal is idempotent per (sourceType, sourceId, eventKind).

New system accounts WAGES and EMPLOYER_PAYROLL_TAXES come from the system chart with Schedule C lines 26 and 23; the migration adds them to existing installs guarded by account role, never duplicating.

Nothing is filed or submitted to any agency, and no payroll is calculated in the app; DQ-CMP-PAYROLL-HOW governs that future build. No SSN or employee-level personal data is accepted, stored or logged — provider summary totals only.

outcome: Hiring readiness, built ahead of the first hire by owner decision: the six dormant payroll obligations wake from the employees fact, the Colorado new-hire report obligation joins them with its 20-day deadline from the first employee's start date, the Compliance screen shows a fact-driven hiring checklist with official links and computed dates, DQ-CMP-PAYROLL-HOW is filed with the payroll-service starting value, and a payroll provider's summary CSV imports into the books as balanced payroll journals so Schedule C and the 941 numbers tie out.

references.purpose: The books posting engine the payroll import posts through: role-based lines, balanced-journal refusal, idempotent per (sourceType, sourceId, eventKind), closed-month placement.

risk: Payroll money figures enter the books from an owner-supplied CSV: a wrong file would post wrong journals. Mitigated by strict balance validation per row, whole-file duplicate protection, the books engine's own balanced-journal refusal, and journal memos naming the import; entries stay reversible through the books like any other journal. No tax is calculated, withheld, deposited or filed by this card.
